Once the target object is located, take it and carry it directly to the specified destination receptacle. For cool-then-place tasks, be aware that navigating to the cooling appliance (e.g., fridge) first to search for the target can also add unnecessary steps if the target is actually located at or near the destination receptacle rather than inside the cooling appliance. Be aware that multiple open cooking surfaces may need to be inspected if the first one does not hold the target, but this still avoids the interaction cost of opening closed cabinets. For heat-then-place tasks involving food items (e.g., eggs), be aware that navigating to a cold-storage appliance (e.g., fridge) first can similarly add unnecessary steps if the target food item is located on an open surface such as a countertop rather than inside the refrigeration unit. Additionally, for heat-then-place tasks involving egg targets, be aware that strict listed-order traversal can incur substantial overhead if the egg is staged on or near the destination receptacle (e.g., garbagecan); consider checking the destination receptacle early when it is an open container where food items may be staged. For cool-then-place tasks involving food items, note that prioritizing open cooking surfaces (e.g., stoveburners) may add overhead if the food is located on a general countertop rather than a dedicated cooking surface; restrict cooking-surface-first search to food types with strong evidence of staging on burners, and otherwise rely on listed-order traversal. For heat-then-place tasks involving mug targets, be aware that navigating to the heating appliance (e.g., microwave) first to search for the mug can add unnecessary steps if the mug is located on a general surface such as a countertop rather than inside the heating appliance; rely on listed-order traversal as the default for mug targets unless strong evidence indicates staging inside the heating appliance. Preliminary evidence suggests that for mug targets in both heat-then-place and clean-then-place tasks, navigating directly to an available open horizontal surface (e.g., countertop) or a beverage-associated appliance surface (e.g., coffeemachine) first can efficiently locate the mug without the overhead of opening closed receptacles, though this has not yet been formally compared against strict listed-order traversal across multiple episodes. For small dining condiment targets (e.g., saltshakers), be aware that navigating to open horizontal surfaces (e.g., countertops) first can add navigation overhead if the condiment is stored inside a closed receptacle (e.g., cabinet); rely on listed-order traversal as the default for condiment targets unless strong evidence indicates staging on open surfaces. Preliminary evidence also suggests that for leafy vegetable targets (e.g., lettuce) in cool-then-place tasks, navigating directly to an available open horizontal surface (e.g., countertop) first can efficiently locate the target without the overhead of opening closed receptacles, though this has not yet been formally compared against strict listed-order traversal across multiple episodes.
